carousels.name: 3 p*rn triggers you can't avoid and how to handle them

slides.title: 3 p*rn triggers you can't avoid [[— and how to handle them.]]
slides.sub: You can't delete the world. You can change your response.

slides.title: [[Ads]] and billboards
slides.body: Suggestive images show up everywhere. Look away, focus on something specific, keep moving. Don't analyse it.

slides.title: Attractive [[people]]
slides.body: Real people aren't triggers — but a p*rn habit can make your brain treat them like one. See the person, not the body. Then move on.

slides.title: [[Memories]]
slides.body: Old p*rn scenes pop into your head out of nowhere. Don't replay them. Change what you're doing — stand up, talk, move.

carousels.name: 5 signs you're romanticising your p*rn habit (harsh)

slides.title: 5 signs you're romanticising [[your p*rn habit.]]
slides.sub: Nostalgia is the urge in disguise.

slides.title: Signs [[1–3]]
items: You remember the rush, never the crash.
You call it "harmless fun" when you talk about it.

slides.title: Signs [[4–5]]
items: You think about "one last time" as a reward.
You forget why you quit p*rn in the first place.

slides.title: Remember it [[honestly]]
slides.body: The 2 AM guilt. The lies. The wasted weekends. That's the real p*rn habit. Not the highlight reel.

slides.title: Break the [[spell]]
items: Write the real story — the after, not the during.
Talk to someone who knew how bad it got.
Stop calling it fun. Call it what it was.
